title: Dynamic Local Usage: An Accurate Model for Usage of Tile-Internal Wiring in Global Routing
problem: Traditional global routing treats local wiring usage as a pre-estimated constant, ignoring actual wire-shape geometry and packing density, leading to inaccuracies in routing prediction and detailed routing failures.
motivation: Advanced nodes (3nm, 5nm) require accurate pre-detailed-routing routing predictions to minimize vias, DRVs, and timing issues; local wiring modeling is bottleneck.
method: The DLU model calculates how much space wires need inside routing tiles by analyzing their exact shapes and positions, instead of using a fixed guess. It adds tip-to-tip penalty extensions—extra costs when wires come close together—to accurately predict how tightly wires can pack. Routing algorithms then use these real congestion measurements to choose better paths for wires. The model also handles incremental updates, such as when connection points move.
key_novelty: Instead of guessing routing space with fixed estimates, this model measures congestion dynamically based on actual wire shapes and positions.
contributions: Significant reduction in via count after detailed routing
Fewer scenic routes and design-rule violations vs static estimates
Improved timing metrics after detailed routing
Better support for incremental pin-movement changes
Superior results vs industrial global router on 3nm/5nm nodes

metrics.other: reduced vias, design-rule violations, and timing degradation

limitations: Evaluation limited to reported comparison with industrial router; detailed quantitative results not specified.
primary_theme: Dynamic local wiring model for accurate global routing at advanced nodes
